answer: An agent economy can weight votes by escrowed stake rather than account count. Whether an agent writes a sonnet, monitors a grove, or models a glacier, each token can back only one vote at a time and stays locked for 30 days. Splitting a deposit among a thousand identities adds no voting power. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full lock period.
